name: Sandinista ideology
summary: Sandinismo is the nationalist, anti-imperialist and revolutionary-left outlook of the FSLN, drawing its name and symbols from Augusto Sandino's resistance to US occupation and its program from Carlos Fonseca's revival of him. In power from 1979 to 1990 it pledged a mixed economy, political pluralism and non-alignment, carried out land reform and a mass literacy campaign, and mixed Marxist, Cuban-influenced and Christian (liberation theology) currents. Its commitments to pluralism were contested in practice by wartime emergency rule.
scope: The FSLN's Sandinismo as articulated by Sandino (1927 manifesto), Carlos Fonseca, the 1969 Historic Program and the Tercerista leadership (Daniel and Humberto Ortega), and as practised by the revolutionary government of 1979-1990. It excludes the post-2007 personalist Ortega-Murillo rule, which sources describe as a centralised, authoritarian departure, and the pre-1979 Marxist-Leninist factions as separate tendencies.

keyFigures.name: Augusto Sandino
keyFigures.role: Led guerrilla resistance to US occupation in 1927-1933; the movement's namesake and symbol.

keyFigures.name: Carlos Fonseca
keyFigures.role: FSLN founder and principal ideologue who revived Sandino's legacy.

keyFigures.name: Daniel Ortega
keyFigures.role: Tercerista leader and long-time head of the FSLN and of the Nicaraguan government.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The revolutionary government pledged better conditions for ordinary Nicaraguans and treated social provision as a state duty, so public health care fits its program.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The 1979 platform promised better worker conditions and price controls on basic goods; a substantial wage rise follows, though wartime inflation limited it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The junta kept a mixed economy but used price controls and state ownership of Somoza-linked property, so it distrusted unregulated markets.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1979 platform nationalized Somoza-linked property, giving the state large holdings, though the mixed economy kept a private sector.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not specifically documented in the sources; inferred from a redistributive, anti-oligarchy program.

unions-good.rationale: The 1979 platform promised free unionization and Sandinista mass organizations included labor and peasant unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Sandinistas expropriated Somocista and idle land and let the 1986 reform reach even efficient estates for the public interest.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Price controls, nationalizations and state direction of the economy show a preference for tight regulation of large firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: A movement defined by raising popular living standards and literacy rejects cutting welfare as dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Credit and technical aid went to cooperatives and state farms, but the mixed economy kept private ownership alongside, so support is moderate.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: the Sandinista state ran neighbourhood vigilance and a state of emergency in wartime, so security arguments carried weight.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from a socially conservative-leaning revolutionary state that stressed discipline.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between protecting speech and curbing reactionary propaganda.

strong-leader.rationale: Fonseca and the Terceristas stressed collective leadership (the national directorate), though Ortega later centralized; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Sandinismo sought to capture and use the state for revolution, not abolish it.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: the Sandinistas armed a popular militia to defend the revolution against the Contras.

empower-police-military.rationale: Facing the Contra war, the Sandinista Army and security services were greatly expanded and given emergency powers.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not documented; inferred from the Sandinista view of women's emancipation as workforce participation.

decide-locally.rationale: The revolution was run by a national directorate with mass organizations from above; inferred preference for national direction.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not covered in the sources opened; inferred from a revolutionary humanist self-image.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents split: Christian-left strands defend the family, while the party formally backed women's emancipation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not an FSLN priority; the party avoided confronting the Church on moral questions, so inferred opposition.

abortion-legal.rationale: Split: the FSLN never legalised abortion but tolerated therapeutic abortion and defeated a right-to-life amendment in 1986.

more-religion-public.rationale: The party's slogan is Christian, socialist, solidarity and it grew from liberation theology, so religion in public life is welcome.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from anti-oppression ideology; party practice toward Caribbean coast peoples was criticized.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; the program treated women's emancipation as economic equality, not a theory of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Sandino's nationalism defended national honor and sovereignty against foreign domination.

gradual-change.rationale: The Sandinistas won power by armed revolution and sought rapid transformation, not gradual change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from internationalism; the government welcomed refugees from Salvadoran violence in 1980.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sandinista Nicaragua took its case against the US to the ICJ, but its core stance is sovereignty-first; modest support.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and a state-managed economy under embargo.

nation-first.rationale: Sandino's central claim was Nicaraguan sovereignty over foreign interests, though the movement also stressed Central American solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The movement opposed US intervention and championed non-intervention.

limit-growth.rationale: Development oriented; inferred that growth is a goal for a poor country.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a left, state-led outlook.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources describe literacy and education as tools of liberation but never address technology as a cure-all, so adherents have no common line.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from an anti-imperialist, non-aligned stance wary of great-power technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Fonseca and the Terceristas built the movement on armed revolution; Sandino fought an armed war against occupation.

experts-over-public.rationale: Education aimed to build revolutionary consciousness among peasants and give the people a voice, so experts do not outrank the public.

central-planning.rationale: The state directed much of the economy, but the mixed economy kept markets; moderate inferred support.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cooperatives and state farms operating inside a mixed economy match this arrangement.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land policy ran through expropriation and cooperatives rather than taxation, so a single land tax replacing other taxes is inferred as foreign to the program.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from a program aimed at breaking up large estates and Somoza-linked fortunes; no inheritance tax is documented.

basic-income.rationale: The revolution favoured price controls, jobs and public services over unconditional cash; inferred, not documented.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic sovereignty and keeping growth within the state point to protecting domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic sovereignty in most sectors was meant to keep growth within the state; credit and investment were channelled to state firms.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Fonseca held that peasants should own the land they work, though state farms and cooperatives were favoured in practice.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: a state-managed economy has no place for abolishing central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Mass organizations tied to the party resemble corporatism but it is not a stated doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Contested: the junta pledged pluralism and universal suffrage, but the FSLN dominated the state in practice.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Sandino spoke from the oppressed against oligarchs; a hereditary monarchy has no place in the movement.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1979 program pledged pluralism, universal suffrage and free elections, but the movement stressed popular (participatory) democracy over procedure.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1979 program promised elections and the movement spoke of popular participation, but nothing documents referendums on laws; adherents split.

workers-councils.rationale: Mass organizations were consultative bodies; no commitment to council power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from nationalism; the Atlantic Coast autonomy dispute shows unwillingness to allow secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Sandino's identification with the oppressed against oligarchs rejects natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The FSLN was founded on armed struggle in the line of Sandino's guerrilla war, so it cannot hold that political violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not a stated view; the revolution fought defensive wars but did not glorify war.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Christian-left strand integrates faith and politics; liberation theology priests held government posts.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Faith inspired the movement but the state was not a theocracy; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A state-led revolution rejects privatizing courts and defense.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred; the movement built a large army but framed it as defensive.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Sandino appealed to an Indo-Hispanic race and the oppressed of all kinds, not a single ethnic nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fonseca drew on Marxist classics and Terceristas named capitalism the main obstacle to social progress, though Sandinismo stressed anti-imperialism above class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Redistribution and land reform point toward greater equality, though not a stated doctrine of equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous Caribbean coast peoples later received autonomy statutes; adherents divided in practice.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and Sandino's complaints about US domination.

civilizational-union.rationale: Sandino called for the union of Central Americans and the Indo-Hispanic race against US imperialism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The revolution and its Christian-socialist slogan stress solidarity over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; communitarian solidarity coexists with a rights language.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses nature's value; Christian-left and Marxist strands could differ.

limit-population.rationale: Ortega in 1987 attacked family planning as an imperialist plot and argued for more births.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: A development-oriented movement; industrialization was a goal.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: a movement that prized education and national sovereignty over disruptive change is unlikely to endorse speeding up disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a social-solidarity outlook.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on popular participation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred: the security state in wartime favored state surveillance powers.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement aimed to overthrow the Somoza order and build a new one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Sandinismo was explicitly an ideology; adherents defend its principles over pure pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Armed struggle came first, but after 1979 the party contested elections and governed; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between principle and wartime necessity.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A movement organizing peasant land reform and literacy for development has no interest in returning to hunter-gatherer life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marxist classics influenced Fonseca, but the movement's concrete program (state farms, unions) kept occupational roles; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Marxist-inspired but mixed economy; distribution by need was a long-run ideal at most.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from socialist and Marxist influences, tempered by a mixed economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Fonseca drew on Marxist classics, and Terceristas called capitalism the main obstacle to progress.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Terceristas backed a gradual popular-democratic phase and alliances with non-revolutionary sectors rather than proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Individual peasants got little land and wanted plots, but state farms dominated; Fonseca favoured peasants owning their land.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Sandino framed US intervention as imperialism; anti-imperialist reading of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-led revolution that financed literacy and land reform through public power rejects the libertarian charge that taxation is theft.

harm-principle.rationale: The 1982-88 state of emergency suspended freedoms for national defence, going beyond harm-prevention, though the Sandinistas defended it as wartime necessity.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective mass organizations and community emphasis; inferred.

conscription.rationale: The Sandinista government introduced military service during the Contra war.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The 1979 program pledged suffrage and elections as the means of accountability, so voting matters more than the right to leave.

state-as-business.rationale: A state-led revolution rejects market-style government.

positive-liberty.rationale: Literacy campaigns and land reform expressed freedom as access to material and educational means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from class analysis that places economic elites first.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Sandino spoke for the Indo-Hispanic race and oppressed; racial hierarchy rejected.

organic-representation.rationale: Mass organizations functioned like functional representation, but no stated doctrine.

total-state.rationale: The junta formally pledged pluralism and a mixed economy; the state did not claim to direct all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Sandino's call to redeem the nation from foreign domination is rebirth-like, though not decadence rhetoric.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Sandino insisted his forces would not invade neighbours; the movement defends sovereignty.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Sandino contrasted the people with oligarchs; feudal ties rejected.

bound-labor.rationale: The 1969 program aimed to liquidate the latifundio; feudal land ties were targets.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Education was used to build revolutionary consciousness, but not framed philosophically.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Christian-left and Marxist strands pull in opposite directions.

single-common-good.rationale: Sandino spoke for the oppressed as one people against oligarchs, but the 1979 program also pledged pluralism; adherents are split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; Third World solidarity and PLO ties lead to inferred opposition.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The 1980 ratification of the refugee convention shows welcome to refugees, but no diaspora-return doctrine is documented.

revive-national-language.rationale: No source records a language revival aim; Spanish is the national language and Caribbean languages were treated separately.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Cooperatives and worker unions were encouraged, but state management dominated.

school-vouchers.rationale: The state's literacy and education drive was public; vouchers conflict with it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Government spending on social programs ran large deficits and inflation was a criticism.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Sandinista state restricted market freedoms while claiming political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The 1979 program pledged laws, a constitution and elections, so rule by moral example alone is not the model.

national-self-determination.rationale: Sandino rejected the loss of Nicaragua's right to govern itself and called sovereignty his cause.

force-without-un.rationale: Nicaragua sued the US at the ICJ and favoured international law over unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Christian-left strand and liberation theology make faith a political resource.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The government welcomed Salvadoran refugees in 1980 and ratified the UN Refugee Convention, so welfare limited to citizens is inferred as disliked.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from a program of expanding social provision without conditions; not documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Split: the Terceristas sought tactical alliances across classes, yet saw capitalism as an obstacle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Sandino's cause was defending national honor and heritage; destroying inherited institutions runs against it.

dominated-front.rationale: Sandino called on Central Americans and the Indo-Hispanic race to unite against the US.

workers-nation.rationale: Fonseca drew on Marxist classics while the movement rested on national sovereignty, so adherents are split on class versus national organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The 1969 program called for women's equality and AMNLAE was a mass organization.

ban-interest.rationale: The state ran nationalized banks in a mixed economy; interest was not targeted, so a ban is inferred as foreign to the program.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Sandino appealed to all the oppressed; segregation conflicts.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist influence on Fonseca and the Terceristas; the Somoza state was seen as a class and imperial instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred: a poor country aiming at development and economic sovereignty would favour domestic energy production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The government welcomed refugees; assimilation demands are inferred as contrary to its solidarity language.

elite-replacement.rationale: Replacement theories are absent from Sandino's anti-imperialism and the FSLN program, which target oligarchs and foreign powers.

proportional-representation.rationale: The 1979 program pledged pluralism; Nicaragua used proportional representation in the 1984 election.

national-mission.rationale: Sandino defended sovereignty rather than exporting a system, though the revolution was a model for others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The 1969 program saw women's emancipation as a key issue; later FSLN proclamations treated women's problems as society-wide.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Sandino denounced the Chamorro and Diaz governments as traitors and the oligarchs as indifferent.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Sandino spoke for the oppressed and the movement's literacy and health programs aimed at lifting all; eugenics is foreign to it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The revolution overthrew the Somoza National Guard; support for accountability is inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The 1979 platform nationalized property and set price controls, a far larger state role than minimal government.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Sandino's appeal to the Indo-Hispanic race presents mixed heritage as the national identity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1979 programme pledged political pluralism, universal suffrage and an end to discrimination (s4), and Sandino spoke for the oppressed of the Indo-Hispanic race.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Terceristas sought a gradual national democratic phase, not world revolution first.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Sandino's anti-imperialism treats foreign domination as colonial; adherents would read settler displacement similarly, though not documented.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: No source documents a Sandinista position on religious versus common civil law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The government avoided restricting the Church or religion; religious freedom was part of the movement's Christian-left outlook.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A ban reflects Hindu-nationalist concerns absent from Sandinismo; inferred rejection.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Christian-left strand and ties to the Church make strict separation unlikely.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Facing Contra war, the state centralized under emergency.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1979 program pledged elections and universal suffrage.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic sovereignty favours domestic production, but the junta needed imports and aid; no documented export-surplus aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Not part of the program; the Miskito relocation drew criticism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Armed insurrection against Somoza and revolutionary war contradict it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The party's slogan is Christian, socialist, solidarity; social-Darwinist competition is rejected.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The 1979 program banned only promoters of a return to Somoza rule; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Sandino's complaint about domination by foreign power resembles non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Pledged pluralism but Council of State dominated by mass organizations.

vanguard-party.rationale: Fonseca and the FSLN were a vanguard led by the national directorate.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Sandino said his greatest honor was to come from the oppressed; the program prioritized the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy not addressed by Sandinismo; no stance.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The 1979 platform promised free unionization, though the emergency restricted strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Ortega in 1987 rejected family planning as an imperialist plot.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Sandino united Nicaraguans, Central Americans and the Indo-Hispanic race as one struggle, treating diversity as a basis of solidarity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The 1979 program pledged elections; lottery for offices is inferred as foreign.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: A state of emergency from 1982 to 1988 curtailed civil liberties.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The 1979 platform called for price controls on basic goods.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mixed: the state of emergency imposed censorship, but the party tolerated La Prensa for periods and pledged pluralism.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army was called the Sandinista Popular Army; party control was criticized.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the welcome given to refugees; long waits conflict with that solidarity.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Sandino presented himself as an artisan from the oppressed; inferred sympathy for leaders paid like workers.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The FSLN was a vanguard led by a national directorate, where decisions bound members after debate.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sandino's sovereignty focus; though Central American unity was supported.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The junta replaced the National Guard with a nonpartisan army; command arrangements were not specified, and the constitution later created a presidency with strong powers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The liberation theology strand opposed hierarchical church control.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement included priests in government, but the state was not a clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Sandino's cause was patriotic defence of the nation, not defeatism; the Terceristas also allied across classes.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The emergency censored news, but art censorship for virtue is not documented; inferred opposition.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed within the scope: the 1979-1990 revolution set no doctrine on term limits, and the 2009 removal of limits under Ortega falls outside the profile and divided former Sandinistas.

recall-officials.rationale: The movement's rhetoric of ruling from below supports recall, though not documented as a mechanism.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The platform focused on land and price controls, not abolishing renting; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Peasants were the core of Fonseca's strategy, but no source claims rural life is morally healthier.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Central American unity was an aim in the 1969 program, but not a reunification of a divided nation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not a stated view; the Sandinistas used education to free minds.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Sandino's Indo-Hispanic race defended Latin American culture.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: Sandinista Nicaragua abolished the death penalty.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Education aimed to build revolutionary consciousness and literacy; creationism is not part of it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not documented; the Christian-left strand might support limits, the secular strand not.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The movement welcomed refugees and stressed popular belonging over blood; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Caribbean coast autonomy came later; the government eventually supported coast languages in schools; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: No documented stance; revolutionary discipline pulls against it, liberation pulls for it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Sandino's concern that foreign finance, such as a canal deal, makes Nicaragua tributary supports cancelling debts to rich lenders.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Sandino warned a US-controlled canal would make Nicaragua dependent.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1979 program promised free elections and later a constitution; a democratically elected assembly drafted the 1987 constitution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The 1979 program pledged pluralism, and limits in practice were justified by war, not growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and the welcome extended to Salvadoran refugees.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: A non-aligned small country with a defensive army would not seek nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Nicaraguan constitution used direct election of the president in 1984.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The nationalized banking system and state economic direction contradict central-bank independence; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Sandino's sovereignty focus gives no basis for land-claim absolutism; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The 1969 program aimed at the latifundio and the 1981 law allowed expropriating idle land.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Sandinista government received Soviet bloc support and Cuban example, so calling the USSR state-capitalist is unlikely.

collective-defense.rationale: The junta committed to nonalignment, so treating an attack on one ally as an attack on all binds it to blocs it avoided.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Sandino treated the US presence as an illegitimate invasion without Nicaraguan consent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Sandinista government avoided confrontation with the Church and had priests in office, rather than curbing it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was an FSLN leader in practice; nonpartisan symbolic heads are inferred as foreign.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and the response to Atlantic Coast autonomy demands; not documented.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nothing documents a one-country-two-systems stance; Atlantic Coast autonomy is partly analogous.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sandino as a man of the oppressed rejects sacred rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A redistributive program of land reform and price controls would not favour flat taxes.

character-from-environment.rationale: Fonseca's emphasis on education to free peasants' minds treats character as formed by circumstances.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred: a poor-country movement focused on literacy and land had no interest in space.

leader-cult.rationale: The Sandinistas honored Sandino and Fonseca in public life.

equal-parenting.rationale: No documented stance; the FSLN avoided family-law disputes.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist classics influenced Fonseca, but the Sandinistas did not declare a socialist state, so the question was not theirs.

land-redistribution.rationale: The 1969 program aimed to liquidate the latifundio, and the 1981 law expropriated idle land.

refugee-return.rationale: The government ratified the UN Refugee Convention in 1980, implying support for refugees' rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Sandino said his forces would not invade neighbouring states.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Sandinistas courted believers and accepted religious freedom; punishing apostasy is foreign to this.

women-must-cover.rationale: The 1969 program called for women's emancipation and equality; compulsory covering contradicts that.

common-currency.rationale: Sandino called for Central American unity, but no currency union stance is documented.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Sandino appealed to Nicaraguans, Central Americans and the Indo-Hispanic race as one people, and the 1969 program called for Central American unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: No documented stance; Atlantic Coast autonomy was fought over.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fonseca used Marxist classics but Sandinismo was not strictly materialist.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: a state that nationalized Somoza-linked holdings and set price controls would back breaking up concentrated economic power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: a state-led mixed economy intervenes to keep key enterprises running, so a no-bailout rule is unlikely.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Equality for women was in the 1969 program and AMNLAE was a mass organization, so parity quotas are inferred as acceptable even though practice lagged.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: revolutionary legitimacy rested on popular will, though the 1979 program also pledged pluralism, so support is mild.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic sovereignty was a goal, but the government sought trade and aid from several blocs rather than a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from a pro-labor, anti-imperialist outlook that favours conditions on trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from Cuban influence and revolutionary mobilization such as the literacy campaign, though wartime shortages forced material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Fonseca revived Sandino and favoured a rural foco-style armed struggle, and the FSLN's small armed core built the insurrection against Somoza.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Sandino set the oppressed against the oligarchs, and the revolution overthrew the Somoza dynasty.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Sandino's legacy and image were the core of revolutionary education; inferred support for national-centred history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Sandino denounced US occupation as an invasion and defended Nicaragua's right to rule itself.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education was meant to free peasants' minds and build revolutionary consciousness around Sandino's legacy and national sovereignty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from support for correcting oppression; not discussed in sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: No source documents a Sandinista position on who should create money; adherents have no clear line.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Terceristas named capitalism the main obstacle to social progress, which implies it does not resolve its crises; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Sandino fought imperial influence over Nicaragua, so cultivating influence in former imperial domains runs against the creed.

delink-world-market.rationale: The junta committed to a mixed economy and non-alignment, trading with several blocs, not breaking ties with rich countries.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: No source documents a stance; Marxist influences and Third Worldism pull one way, a pro-worker solidarity stance the other.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Sandino spoke as one of the oppressed against privilege, and the 1979 program banned ideological discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1979 program pledged pluralism and suffrage; a constitutional rights charter fits, though not documented in sources opened.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Sandino rejected arrangements that ceded Nicaraguan sovereignty to the US, such as the canal deal, so he would reject imposed treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The 1979 program pledged universal suffrage and free elections, and the Somoza dynasty was the revolution's target.

minority-veto.rationale: A vanguard party using party discipline would not let a dissenting minority block decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The FSLN fought the Somoza dictatorship by arms and claimed Sandino's mantle.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The junta pledged pluralism, but power sat with the national directorate and mass organizations, so adherents were split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses animals; no distinct Sandinista position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses animals; no distinct Sandinista position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Sandino framed liberation as the oppressed's own work, not charity from elites.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A committed armed and political movement whose cadres were expected to participate.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: education was meant to free minds and build consciousness, implying distrust of media that pacify.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The movement was Marxist-influenced but no source documents a hegemony theory; split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Sandino warned that a US-controlled canal would make Nicaragua dependent and tributary, an early dependency view.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with refugees and internationalist volunteers; not documented.

party-own-road.rationale: The Terceristas shaped a distinctly Latin American socialism, adopting Sandino and the Cuban example over Moscow's line.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The junta sought aid and trade from several blocs and the literacy campaign drew international support, so it did not insist on self-reliance alone.

return-lost-territory.rationale: No source documents a stance on recovering lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not stated; the movement saw itself as mestizo and 'Indo-Hispanic', and Caribbean coast peoples distrusted it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from a left identity; not documented.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: A Marxist-influenced movement allied with Cuba and the USSR would reject equating communism with fascism; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred; a left, anti-oppression movement would reject this.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The movement toppled Somoza monuments and honored its own heroes; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Women's emancipation was the FSLN's gender priority; equal attention to men's disadvantage is not documented.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The FSLN framed women's problems as society-wide, so symmetry claims are inferred as unwelcome.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Terceristas shaped a distinct Latin American socialism, implying institutions can fit local conditions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army was the party's own Sandinista army, but no source documents a guardian doctrine.

paid-care-work.rationale: The FSLN treated emancipation as workforce participation, not paid care, so split.

filial-duty.rationale: No source documents a stance; Christian-left strand supports it, secular strand indifferent.

office-by-exam.rationale: Revolutionary cadres, not examinations, filled posts; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic sovereignty in most sectors was meant to keep growth within the state.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: No source documents a stance; the party avoided confronting the Church on family law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rhetoric of popular participation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred: a state-led social program rejects privatized pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Fonseca wanted peasants to own the land they work, but state farms and cooperatives were favoured; split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The junta promised elections and a constitution; inferred acceptance of parliamentary budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: The government recognised Caribbean coast languages; inferred from the autonomy dispute.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Economic sovereignty and nationalist focus point to limiting foreign land ownership; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: No documented stance; legal debate foreign to Sandinismo.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from Christian-socialist solidarity and austerity of wartime economy.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The party condemned US arming of the Contras and an ICJ ruling found the US violated international law, though Nicaragua was accused of aiding Salvadoran rebels.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Sandinistas opposed foreign intervention and the ICJ found the US violated international law in Nicaragua.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-imperialism targeted foreign corporate and state influence; inferred agreement that corporations dominate politics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sandinismo prized national sovereignty, and the Ortega government later restricted foreign-funded NGOs.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Ortega in 1987 attacked family planning as an imperialist plot and argued for more births.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from a program of better worker conditions and state employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Sandino saw the US, a democracy, as an invader; inferred scepticism.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Revolutionaries disobeyed Somoza but demanded obedience to their own government; split.

non-intervention.rationale: Sandino rejected US intervention and the Sandinista government took the US to the ICJ over the Contras, but the FSLN government itself aided the FMLN in El Salvador.

industrial-unions.rationale: No documented stance on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Sandino addressed all Nicaraguans and the oppressed; conspiracy theories about minorities are not part of the program.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The FSLN avoided confronting the Church on family matters, so abolishing legal marriage is unlikely.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The state of emergency imposed censorship, though pluralism was pledged; split.

local-production.rationale: Economic sovereignty favours domestic production, but no documented localism.

informal-organisation.rationale: The FSLN was a disciplined vanguard organization with a national directorate, not informal affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Nicaragua took its case to the ICJ and appealed to international law against the US.

religious-nation.rationale: The movement's Christian-left strand welcomed believers but the nation was defined by sovereignty and class, not a shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Sandino rejected tribute to a dominating power and called for unity against it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: a centralizing state directed investment nationally.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The government kept a mixed economy with private ownership; personal property was not targeted.

defeat-communism.rationale: The party was aligned with Cuba and the Soviet bloc and drew on Marxism; opposition to this is inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: A mixed economy was pledged, but social services were run by the state; split.

religion-illusion.rationale: The party's slogan is Christian and socialist, and liberation theology was central.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Terceristas called capitalism the main obstacle to progress while backing a popular-democratic phase with non-revolutionary sectors; split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1969 program saw emancipation largely as full participation in the workforce, tying it to economic change.

socialized-care.rationale: No source documents it; emancipation was framed through workforce participation.

purge-loanwords.rationale: No language purism is documented in the movement.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from support for Atlantic Coast autonomy and sovereignty, though not documented.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperatives were favoured by the state, but the revolution did not seek small self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: Sandinista settlement and relocation drew Miskito criticism, so majority settlement is unlikely.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The 1979 program's mixed economy and non-alignment resemble a third way, but Marxism influenced Fonseca; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Sandino's claim to the land rested on defending his country, not historic or religious tie against residents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of the program; a left movement would reject denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Party avoided confronting conservative religious opinion; no documented position, so inferred opposition to criminalization.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 1979 program pledged pluralism, though the 1982-88 emergency curtailed freedoms.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the party courted Christians but was not theocratic.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Sandino opposed foreign domination and the exploitation of Nicaragua's wealth for others.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious doctrine foreign to the movement, but resistance to invasion was a Sandinista duty; split.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Sandinista government was not religious-law based and neither fought unreligious rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The party's mass organizations and its claim to rule from below show a participatory ideal, though real power stayed centralized.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The party's gender framing was workforce participation; split.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not documented; inferred as unlikely given party's caution on social questions.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the Christian-left strand and the party's caution toward Church positions.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The FSLN identifies as socialist and Christian left, so it sees the left as meaningful.

alienated-labor.rationale: Fonseca used Marxist classics but no source documents alienation theory.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not part of the program; Sandino's solidarity with the oppressed contradicts it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority came from the people in the 1979 program, though liberation theology gave faith political roles.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: No documented stance; Christian-left ties make a ban unlikely.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the 1969 program's women's equality; not documented.

social-market-economy.rationale: A mixed economy was pledged, similar in spirit, but with state ownership and planning beyond social market.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Sandinistas built a large army during the Contra war.

rich-first.rationale: The 1969 program aimed to liquidate the latifundio; uneven growth was not an aim.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The July 1979 government program committed to a nonaligned foreign policy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Sandino set the oppressed against oligarchs; the movement overthrew a dynasty, though the later Ortega rule has dynastic features.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-imperialist economic sovereignty makes austerity conditions unwelcome; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The July 1979 program pledged universal suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: No documented stance; ecofeminism is not in the sources.

reification.rationale: Marxist classics influenced Fonseca but the concept is not documented.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A movement of the oppressed that saw elites controlling media; inferred, also used to justify press curbs.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1979 program pledged pluralism, but emergency decrees were common.

racial-franchise.rationale: The July 1979 program pledged universal suffrage, and Sandino addressed all Nicaraguans.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the Sandinista program predates the internet.

open-government-data.rationale: The state of emergency imposed censorship; no documented stance.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The government avoided religious restrictions; inferred rejection.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Sandino's address to all Nicaraguans and the oppressed contradicts minority boycotts.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Liberation theology reads Christianity through the lens of the poor, a modern reinterpretation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sandino contrasted oligarchs with the oppressed, and the movement targeted concentrated Somoza wealth.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The party's slogan is Christian, socialist, solidarity.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A state-building revolution expanded security services.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Atlantic Coast autonomy question showed ambivalence; split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: A state-led social program rejects charity as the main route.

term-limits.rationale: Ortega overturned term limits in 2009, but older adherents opposed; split but inferred mild opposition.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: No documented stance; liberation theology priests were male Catholics.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1969 program called for ending discrimination against women and equality in economic, political and cultural life.

rent-control.rationale: Price controls on basic goods were in the 1979 platform; inferred extension to rents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Sandinista Youth organization and militia mobilised young people; inferred mild support.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Non-alignment suggests rejecting great-power bases and weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Non-alignment was a pledge of the junta, and Sandino fought the US military presence.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with victims of oppression; not documented.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marxist influence on the movement gave an anti-rentier view of income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Sandino fought a defensive war against occupation, and the FSLN held armed defence legitimate.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Sandino's lineage claims continuity with national resistance, but no ancient-origin doctrine.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The movement honoured Sandino, Fonseca and fallen fighters as martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Liberation theology frames politics as moral struggle, but Marxists differ; split.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement prioritized seizing power and then cultural projects such as literacy.

god-not-male.rationale: No documented stance; liberation theology's views vary.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Atlantic Coast autonomy is relevant but no documented stance.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The program kept a mixed economy with wages, prices and private firms; abolishing money is a distant communist goal the movement never pursued.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The 1979 program pledged pluralism, elections and a constitution, and the movement was born opposing the Somoza dictatorship's arbitrary rule.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic liquid-democracy idea; no documented stance, though the movement spoke of popular participation.

independent-unions.rationale: Sandinista mass organisations, including the unions, were tied to the FSLN and sat in the Council of State as its allies rather than as independent bodies.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist and Cuban-influenced currents, which held that revolution must put workers and peasants in power; the sources do not state this test.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the revolutionary government's treatment of social provision as a state duty and its mixed economy with a large public sector.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: the revolutionary government governed through a single Council of State and later one assembly; the sources do not discuss chambers.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the program favoured state, cooperative and private property in a mixed economy, not ownership by municipalities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the vanguard-led, centralised party structure of the FSLN; the sources do not discuss confederations.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the aim of better conditions for working families; the sources discuss women's emancipation through work but not a family wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not touch medical regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not touch ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from state control of banking and foreign exchange under the revolutionary government; no source states this.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: the 1979-1990 movement predates the internet and its principles give no direction.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: Christian and pluralist currents value the person, while the revolution subordinated individuals to national defence and emergency rule; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Christian and liberation-theology currents within the FSLN, which treated faith as part of social liberation.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: the government was centralised but later granted the Atlantic Coast an autonomy statute, so adherents' practice points both ways.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred: the movement predates genetic engineering and its principles give no direction.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred: the sources say nothing on density; its agrarian-reform focus gives no direction.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: Sandinismo organised by class and nation, not by race, though it later addressed Atlantic Coast indigenous claims.

racial-pride.rationale: Sandino's manifesto appeals to Indo-Hispanic pride and unity, so ancestry pride fits, though it is not racial pride as such.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialism and non-alignment, with armed force framed as resisting foreign intervention.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Sandino appealed to the Indo-Hispanic peoples and the 1969 program to Central American unity across borders, so shared heritage over state lines fits, though language is not stated as the test.

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1979 program promised universal suffrage and political pluralism in common elections, which leaves no room for confessional electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Sandinismo defined itself against US intervention and interference, so a sense of outside hostility is natural, but partition of Nicaragua specifically is not a stated theme; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: The revolutionary government treated education as a public duty and expanded free schooling through its literacy campaign, so free public tuition follows.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not addressed; a state-directed mixed economy suggests preferring public planning and regulation to price instruments, inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; land reform and the revolution's appeal to future social justice suggest mild agreement with a duty to later generations, inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Sandinista women's policy stressed equal workforce participation and emancipation, not distinct feminine values in politics; inferred from that framing.

arms-reduction.rationale: The government built a large army under Contra war while pursuing non-alignment and peace diplomacy, so adherents split on arms levels; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Non-alignment and sovereignty claims in the program suggest support for open dealings between states, though secret diplomacy is not discussed; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: A mixed economy with a leading state role suggests support for state control over capital flows, though the sources do not discuss capital controls; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed directly; the revolutionary government built a national army and police while arming popular militias, so adherents are inferred to favour a state armed force with the militias absorbed into it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialist, defensive war stance: Sandinistas fought a war against the Contras and backed conscription, but opposed wars of intervention.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Sandinista mass organisations included unions that held seats in the Council of State, and the government pledged a mixed economy with a strong labour role.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; the government preferred land reform, subsidies and public services over tax credits, but it is not stated.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from state-led development and deficit spending in the 1980s, which a binding limit would contradict; not stated in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Anti-imperialism and non-alignment were central, and the government pushed for a new international economic order in favour of developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The FSLN took over the state in 1979 and built on it, though it restructured institutions; Marxist currents spoke of a revolutionary state, but the practice was to take power and use it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The government pledged a mixed economy and pluralism, with no fixed blueprint; inferred from that pledge rather than a direct statement.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; the 1980s ideology pre-dates ecological economics.

sacred-nation.rationale: Nationalism and the memory of Sandino as a national hero give the nation lasting meaning, but 'sacred' is stronger than the sources state; Christian currents partly support it.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; the government's priorities were land reform and literacy, and debt relief is not documented.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: Sandino and the 1969 programme describe foreign and metropolitan exploitation of Nicaragua, but regional internal colonialism is only loosely implied.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Christian liberation-theology currents and humanist rhetoric imply a shared human dignity, though Marxist currents treat human nature as historical; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: The revolutionary government supported media in service of the revolution and was not committed to independence from government; adherents are inferred to back public media, with the independence clause at odds with practice.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred as split: liberation-theology Christians and secular Marxists both sat within Sandinismo, with no shared view on this.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the land reform and mixed-economy programme, which favoured peasants and cooperatives with state credit and prices.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from its non-aligned, anti-imperialist stance; nuclear arms were not a Sandinista issue.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the FSLN's self-presentation as the party of workers and peasants, though it saw itself as a broader front.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to women's equality in law; the practice was not an issue in Nicaragua.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from its revolutionary commitment to women's legal equality and the women's organisation AMNLAE, including access to land under agrarian reform.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; no position follows from its principles.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from its state-directed mixed economy, which favours public regulation over private liability.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred as split: the 1980s government granted Atlantic Coast autonomy but kept lawmaking in elected national bodies.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; development and anti-imperialist goals competed with any environmental priority.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the 1979 abolition of the death penalty and the revolution's rehabilitative penal policy.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; Nicaragua was a country of emigration and no position follows from its principles.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the Sandinistas' reliance on state-aligned mass organisations and the workers' central, the CST; an opt-out right is not discussed in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the 1979 program's universal suffrage (s4) and the Sandinista state's civil registry; identification at the polls is not discussed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Christian currents within Sandinismo and its Church relations (s6); no interpretation of a religion was given legal precedence in the program.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The 1979 program pledged pluralism and elections (s4), but Sandinismo spoke of participatory revolutionary democracy and wartime emergency rule; inferred, since adherents split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the Sandinista programme of women's emancipation (s6); sexual morality is not discussed directly and the Catholic currents dissented.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the 1979 program's pledge of pluralism and civil liberties (s4), weighed against wartime censorship.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the revolution's preference for state-provided services, price controls and land reform over cash replacing welfare; not discussed in the sources.

women-suffrage.rationale: The July 1979 program committed to universal suffrage, and Sandinismo treated women's emancipation as part of the revolution.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the strong liberation theology wing within Sandinismo; the sources show tension with the Church over abortion and family planning but no claim that religion is a major cause of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Sandino's appeal to Indo-Hispanic unity and the program's anti-discrimination aims; racial science is not discussed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the Sandinista women's association and state emphasis on emancipation (s6); dedicated government agencies are not described.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the land reform, which redistributed land through the state and cooperatives rather than recognising first-come private claims.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: the FSLN invoked international law against the US at the World Court but was wary of outside bodies judging revolutionary leaders; adherents would split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the Christian-Marxist current: liberation theology read scripture through the lens of the poor rather than as literal inerrancy.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The FSLN backed women's equality and a women's mass organisation, so adherents would want it written into any self-rule arrangement.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: Sandinismo pledged a mixed economy, not a nationalised planned one, so the question fits it poorly.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the revolution ran direct national elections in 1984 and its program stressed popular participation rather than delegate chains.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: the revolutionary government kept church and state separate and clashed with the Catholic hierarchy, though it courted Christian supporters.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the 1980s turn to autonomy for the Atlantic Coast peoples after conflict with the Miskito; not cited in the sources held here.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: Sandinismo was anti-imperialist and pro self-determination, but no source addresses local plebiscites over disputed territory.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: Sandinista nationalism defended Nicaragua's existing sovereign territory, and Latin American states broadly kept inherited borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: the program aimed at development, literacy and better living standards rather than limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: Sandinista policy toward Indigenous peoples shifted over the decade and sources here do not address settlement limits.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the 1983 national service law drafted men while women served as volunteers, though some adherents wanted equal service.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Sandinismo draws on Sandino's defence of Nicaraguan soil against occupation and a nationalist tie to the land, though the sources do not call the tie spiritual.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Sandinistas abolished the death penalty and stressed revolutionary legality, though wartime emergency rule was harsh; inferred, so low.

close-ties-china.rationale: Sandinismo was anti-imperialist and non-aligned and leaned on Cuba and the Soviet bloc, not China; it did not seek China as a main partner.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Anti-imperialist nationalism would support kin abroad in principle, but Nicaragua's neighbours were not a Sandinista concern; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The agrarian reform and nationalised property treated land and resources as the people's common wealth, as the sources on the reform describe.

self-ownership.rationale: The program prized collective and social ends over individual ownership, so strong self-ownership is not a Sandinista claim; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not discuss consumption taxes, and the government's price controls and subsidies pull in different directions.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The Sandinistas stressed universal programs such as the literacy and health campaigns rather than means-tested help.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The FSLN built mass organisations and a vanguard party tied to the people, not a leader bypassing groups, as the sources describe.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Anti-oligarchic nationalism opposed privileges for the Somoza-connected business class, though the Sandinistas themselves favoured state firms; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Christian base communities and liberation theology sat inside the movement and the program called for pluralism rather than denominational organisation; the stance on denominational parties is inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The sources do not address combining technology with ancestral values, and adherents' treatment of indigenous heritage varied.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Sandinistas promoted women's equality through the women's association and family law reform, so a wife's right to divorce fits; the sources do not mention divorce specifically.

national-resource-control.rationale: National control of resources and anti-foreign-exploitation was core to the Sandinista program, as the sources on the revolution and land reform describe.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The 1969 program aimed to liquidate the latifundio, which treats the pattern of landholding as unjust regardless of how it arose.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the anti-imperialist, redistributive programme of the revolutionary government.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the revolutionary-left view that structural inequality holds disadvantaged groups back.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Sandino's appeal to justice and sovereignty against an occupation whose rule he refused to accept.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the programme focuses on land and literacy, not automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: The 1979 programme pledged non-alignment, which favours independent centres of power over a single dominant one.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Marxist influences noted in the ideology.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Sandinismo is a nationalist, anti-imperialist outlook that ties love of country to the cause of peasants and workers.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's framing of women's emancipation through workforce participation and class-based aims.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from the 1979 mixed-economy pledge under FSLN leadership; adherents differed on how far the party should direct it.

missingStatements.text: Peasants and workers should be organised into mass organisations tied to the ruling party.
missingStatements.rationale: Sandinista mass organisations (unions, women's, neighbourhood) held most influence in the Council of State.
missingStatements.declined: Mass organisations tied to the ruling party are a mechanism of one-party rule, already covered by one-party-rule; held at weak value 1.

missingStatements.text: Education should be used to raise the political consciousness of the poor, including through a national literacy campaign.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1980 literacy campaign cut illiteracy from over 50% to about 12%, and Sandinistas saw education as a way to free peasants' minds.
missingStatements.declined: Mass literacy is not contested, and the political-consciousness aim is covered by the statements on class and education; not worth a statement every audit must answer.

missingStatements.text: A country should aim to unite politically with its neighbours in a regional federation against foreign domination.
missingStatements.rationale: Sandino addressed Central Americans and the Indo-Hispanic race, and the 1969 program called for Central American unity.

notes: Practice diverged from stated pluralism: the 1982-88 emergency curtailed freedoms and Ortega's post-2007 rule is described as authoritarian. Many answers are inferences because the movement was a practical revolutionary program, not a systematic doctrine; the unfetched 1969 Historic Program text was known only through secondary sources.
